questions.text: Queen Khizran was the wife of which Abbasid Caliph?
questions.explanation: Queen Khizran was the wife of the third Abbasid Caliph, Al Mehdi. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, abbasid caliphate (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Who was the first great Arab alchemist?
questions.explanation: The first great Arab alchemist was Jabir bin Hayyan, often referred to as the father of chemistry. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, abbasid caliphate (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Ikhwan al-Safa was what type of organization?
questions.explanation: Ikhwan al-Safa was a secret organization of Muslim philosophers and scholars in the 10th century. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, abbasid caliphate (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Who is the author of 'Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb' (The Canon of Medicine)?
questions.explanation: The author of 'Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb' (The Canon of Medicine) is Ibn Sina (Avicenna). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, abbasid caliphate (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: What was the title given to the philosopher Al-Farabi?
questions.explanation: Al-Farabi was given the title "The Second Teacher" (Al-Mu'allim al-Thani), with Aristotle being regarded as the First Teacher. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, abbasid caliphate (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Who is the author of the famous medical encyclopedia 'Al-Hawi'?
questions.explanation: The famous medical encyclopedia 'Al-Hawi' was authored by Abu Bakr Zakaria Razi. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, abbasid caliphate (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Haroon al Rashid was a caliph of which Islamic dynasty?
questions.explanation: Haroon al Rashid was a caliph of the Abbasid dynasty. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, abbasid caliphate.

questions.text: Which companion of the Prophet (PBUH) is known as the Conqueror of Egypt?
questions.explanation: The companion known as the Conqueror of Egypt is Hazrat Amr ibn al-As (R.A). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, administration conquests.

questions.text: Which city served as the first capital of the Rashidun Caliphate?
questions.explanation: The first capital of the Rashidun Caliphate was Madina. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, administration conquests.

questions.text: Which empire ruled Egypt before the Muslim conquest under Hazrat Amr ibn al-Aas (RA)?
questions.explanation: Egypt was under the rule of the Byzantine Empire before the Muslim conquest led by Hazrat Amr ibn al-Aas (RA). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, administration conquests.

questions.text: Where was Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A) elected as the first Caliph of Islam?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A) was elected as the first Caliph of Islam at Saqifah Bani Saedah. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of abu bakr r a (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: During which years did Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) serve as caliph?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) served as caliph from 632-634 A.D. (11-13 A.H.), a period of about 2 years and 3 months. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of abu bakr r a.

questions.text: Who among the following was given the title of 'Sani as Nain'?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was given the title of 'Sani as Nain' (the Second of the Two), as he was the companion of the Prophet (PBUH) in the Cave of Thaur during the Hijrah. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of abu bakr r a.

questions.text: Who was the first caliph of Islam?
questions.explanation: The first caliph of Islam was Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of abu bakr r a.

questions.text: The term 'Khawarij' refers to which group in Islamic history?
questions.explanation: The term 'Khawarij' refers to Rebels — a group that broke away from the mainstream Muslim community during the Caliphate of Ali (R.A). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of ali r a (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: In which year did Hazrat Ali (RA) become Khalifah?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Ali (RA) became the fourth Khalifah of Islam in the year 35 A.H. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of ali r a.

questions.text: On which date was Hazrat Ali (R.A) martyred?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Ali (R.A) was martyred on 21 Ramzan 40 A.H when he was attacked during Fajr prayer in the mosque of Kufa. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of ali r a.

questions.text: In which year was the Battle of Camel fought during the Islamic era?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Camel (Jang-e-Jamal) was fought in 36 A.H between the forces of Caliph Ali (R.A) and those led by Aisha (R.A), Talha (R.A), and Zubair (R.A). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of ali r a.

questions.text: Where is Hazrat Ali ibn Abu Talib (R.A) buried?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Ali ibn Abu Talib (R.A) is buried in Najaf, Iraq. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of ali r a.

questions.text: In which present-day country did the Battle of Siffin take place?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Siffin took place in present-day Syria, near the Euphrates River. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of ali r a.

questions.text: The Battle of Siffin was fought in 37 A.H. between Hazrat Ali (RA) and which notable figure?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Siffin was fought in 37 A.H. between Hazrat Ali (RA) and Hazrat Muawia (RA). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of ali r a.

questions.text: Who established the first organized police department in Islamic history?
questions.explanation: The first organized police department in Islamic history was established by Hazrat Umar (RA). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of umar r a (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: The final battle against the Persian Empire during the reign of Hazrat Umar (R.A) was fought at which location?
questions.explanation: The final decisive battle against the Persian Empire during the reign of Hazrat Umar (R.A) was fought at Nihawand. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of umar r a (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Which Caliph established the institution of Bait Ul Mal for the welfare of the Islamic state?
questions.explanation: Note: Abu Bakr (RA) kept a simple treasury; Umar (RA) set up Bait-ul-Mal as a formal institution with a diwan. The institution of Bait Ul Mal (Public Treasury) was established by Hazrat Umar (RA) during his caliphate. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of umar r a.

questions.text: The Battle of Yarmouk was a significant conflict fought between Muslims and which empire?
questions.explanation: Fixed: Yarmouk (15 AH / 636 AD) was fought against the Byzantine (Eastern Roman) Empire under Heraclius; "Byzantine" is the precise option. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of umar r a.

questions.text: What was the outcome of the Battle of Qadasiyyah for the Muslim army?

options.B: Victory for the Muslims and acquisition of Iraq
options.C: Stalemate and peace treaty with Persia
options.D: Victory but withdrawal due to heavy losses

questions.explanation: The Battle of Qadasiyyah resulted in a decisive victory for the Muslims and acquisition of Iraq. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of umar r a.

questions.text: Which companion of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is famously known as the conqueror of Persia?
questions.explanation: The companion famously known as the conqueror of Persia is Hazrat Saad bin Abi Waqqas (R.A). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of umar r a.

questions.text: Which title is associated with Hazrat Usman (R.A) due to his significant contribution to compiling the Quran?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Usman (R.A) is known as Jami' al-Quran (Compiler of the Quran) for his pivotal role in compiling the Quran into a single standardized book. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of usman r a.

questions.text: On which Islamic date was Hazrat Usman (RA) martyred?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Usman (RA) was martyred on 18th Zul-Hijjah in the year 35 AH. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of usman r a.

questions.text: On which day of the week was Hazrat Usman (RA) martyred?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Usman (RA) was martyred on Friday, the 18th of Dhul-Hijjah, 35 AH. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of usman r a.

questions.text: When was the full invasion of the Sassanid Empire completed?
questions.explanation: The full invasion of the Sassanid Empire was completed in 651 A.D. during the caliphate of Hazrat Usman (R.A). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of usman r a.

questions.text: Which Caliph ordered the distribution of the copies of the Holy Quran to different provinces of the Islamic empire?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Usman (R.A) ordered the distribution of standardized copies of the Holy Quran to different provinces of the Islamic empire. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of usman r a.

questions.text: Who served as the longest-reigning Caliph during the Rashidun Caliphate?
questions.explanation: The longest-reigning Caliph during the Rashidun Caliphate was Hazrat Usman (R.A), who ruled for approximately 12 years. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, caliphate of usman r a.

questions.text: Jamila al-Azhar is located in which city?
questions.explanation: Jamila al-Azhar (Al-Azhar University) is located in Cairo, Egypt. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, fatimid safavid empires (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: The last Fatimid ruler was
questions.explanation: The last Fatimid ruler was Al-Adid, who was deposed by Salahuddin Ayyubi in 1171 CE. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, fatimid safavid empires.

questions.text: The founder of Fatmid dynasty was:
questions.explanation: The founder of the Fatimid dynasty was Al-Mahdi (Ubaydullah al-Mahdi Billah). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, fatimid safavid empires.

questions.text: Al Azhar University is the Chief centre of Islamic and Arabic learning in the world located in the?
questions.explanation: Al Azhar University, the chief centre of Islamic and Arabic learning in the world, is located in Cairo, Egypt. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, fatimid safavid empires.

questions.text: Which scientist is considered the source of European scholars' knowledge regarding light and the eye?
questions.explanation: The scientist considered the source of European scholars' knowledge regarding light and the eye is Ibn al-Haytham. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, fatimid safavid empires (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: In which city is the renowned Islamic university, Al-Azhar University, located?
questions.explanation: Al-Azhar University is located in Cairo, Egypt. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, fatimid safavid empires.

questions.text: What is the meaning of Hijr-e-Aswad?
questions.explanation: Hijr-e-Aswad means the Black Stone, which is set in the eastern corner of the Kaaba. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous islamic history dynasties (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Hassan al-Banna, the founder of the Muslim Brotherhood, was assassinated in which year?
questions.explanation: Hassan al-Banna, the founder of the Muslim Brotherhood (Ikhwan al-Muslimeen), was assassinated in 1949 in Cairo, Egypt. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous islamic history dynasties (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Where was the famous Muslim historian and thinker Ibn Khuldun born?
questions.explanation: Ibn Khuldun, the famous Muslim historian and thinker, was born in Tunisia. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous islamic history dynasties (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: First Islamic summit of OIC was held in which country?
questions.explanation: The first Islamic summit of the OIC was held in Morocco (Rabat) in 1969. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous islamic history dynasties (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: In which year was OIC founded?
questions.explanation: The Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) was founded on September 25, 1969. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous islamic history dynasties (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Who is the author of 'Fusus al-Hikam'?
questions.explanation: The author of 'Fusus al-Hikam' is Ibn Arabi, the renowned Sufi mystic and philosopher. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous islamic history dynasties (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Who initiated the Jihad against the newly introduced religion of Din-e-Illahi?
questions.explanation: Mujadad Alif Sani (Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi) initiated the Jihad against the newly introduced religion of Din-e-Illahi. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, muslim rule in india (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: The book Khutbat-e-Ahmadiya is written by?
questions.explanation: Fixed: "Khutbat-e-Ahmadiya" (1870) is by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan, the Urdu version of his essays on the life of the Prophet (PBUH). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, muslim rule in india (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Who is the author of the book 'Spirit of Islam'?
questions.explanation: The book 'Spirit of Islam' was authored by Syed Ameer Ali. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, muslim rule in india (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Maktoobat e Imam Rabbani is one of the writings of ?
questions.explanation: Maktoobat e Imam Rabbani is one of the writings of Mujaddid Alif Sani (Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, muslim rule in india (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Dars-e-Nizami was launched in:
questions.explanation: Dars-e-Nizami was launched in Lucknow. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, muslim rule in india (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi (Mujaddid Alif Sani) was born on ?
questions.explanation: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi (Mujaddid Alif Sani) was born on 971 AH (1564 CE). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, muslim rule in india (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Who is the author of 'Izhar-ul-Haq'?
questions.explanation: The author of 'Izhar-ul-Haq' is Rahmatullah Kairanawi. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, muslim rule in india (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Who is the author of the treatise 'Risala Ithbat-e-Nubuwwat'?

options.D: Hazrat Mujaddid Alf Thani (Shaykh Ahmad Sirhindi)

questions.explanation: The treatise 'Risala Ithbat-e-Nubuwwat' was authored by Hazrat Mujaddid Alf Thani (Shaykh Ahmad Sirhindi). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, muslim rule in india (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Which Turkish leader is credited with abolishing the Institution of Caliphate?
questions.explanation: The institution of the Caliphate was abolished by Mustafa Kamal Ataturk in 1924. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ottoman empire (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Which Ottoman Sultan was responsible for transferring the Abbasid Caliphate to Istanbul?
questions.explanation: The Ottoman Sultan Salim I was responsible for transferring the Abbasid Caliphate to Istanbul after his conquest of Egypt in 1517 CE. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ottoman empire.

questions.text: Who was the first ruler of the Ottoman Caliphate?
questions.explanation: The first ruler of the Ottoman Caliphate was Usman-I (Osman I), who founded the Ottoman Empire in 1299 CE. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ottoman empire.

questions.text: What was the name of the post-World War One treaty between the Allied powers and the Ottoman government in 1920?
questions.explanation: The post-World War I treaty between the Allied powers and the Ottoman government in 1920 was the Treaty of Sevres. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ottoman empire.

questions.text: In which year was the Treaty of Sevres signed, marking a significant event in the dissolution of the Ottoman Empire?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Sevres was signed in 1920, marking a major step in the dissolution of the Ottoman Empire after World War I. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ottoman empire.

questions.text: Which empire finally ended the Abbasid Caliphate's reign in 1517 CE?
questions.explanation: The Ottoman Empire finally ended the Abbasid Caliphate's reign in 1517 CE when Sultan Selim I conquered Cairo and took the last Abbasid Caliph, Al-Mutawakkil III, to Istanbul. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, ottoman empire.

questions.text: Who was the last ruler of the Umayyad dynasty?
questions.explanation: The last ruler of the Umayyad dynasty was Marwan II (Marwan ibn Muhammad), who ruled from 744 to 750 CE. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, umayyad caliphate (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: How many Umayyad caliphs were there?
questions.explanation: Fixed: the Umayyad dynasty of Damascus had 14 caliphs (Muawiya I to Marwan II), 661–750 AD. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, umayyad caliphate (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Hajjaj bin Yousuf was appointed as the governor of which region during the Umayyad Caliphate?
questions.explanation: Hajjaj bin Yousuf was appointed as the governor of Iraq during the Umayyad Caliphate. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, umayyad caliphate.

questions.text: In which year did the Umayyad Dynasty come to an end?
questions.explanation: The Umayyad Dynasty came to an end in 750 AD when the Abbasids defeated Marwan II at the Battle of the Zab. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, umayyad caliphate.

questions.text: Who led the Muslim conquests into Central Asia during the Umayyad Caliphate?
questions.explanation: The Muslim conquests into Central Asia during the Umayyad Caliphate were led by Qutayba Bin Muslim. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, umayyad caliphate.

questions.text: In which Hijri year did the event of Karbala take place?
questions.explanation: The tragic event of Karbala took place in 61 AH (680 CE), on the 10th of Muharram. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, umayyad caliphate.

questions.text: Who founded the historic city of Kairouan in Tunisia?
questions.explanation: The historic city of Kairouan in Tunisia was founded by Uqba bin Nafey in 678 AD. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, umayyad caliphate.
